scenes.title: Set equality — what equals means in a proof assistant
scenes.visualNotes: 6 beats: textbook SetEq hook, definitional vs propositional equality, homogeneous Lean Eq and Set.ext, notation-backed Turn SetEq, FunctionEq, then isomorphism and higher sameness.

beats.say:
Hi friends, welcome back.
The best way to understand a math concept is to formalize it.
To day we formalize Set equality.
And the textbook definition looks really simple.
Two sets are equal when each one is a subset of the other.
But if we want to formalize this statement,
we need to understand what equals sign actually means inside a proof assistant. This is more complicated than you think.
beats.sayZh: 大家好，欢迎回来。真正理解一个数学概念的最好方式，就是把它形式化。上期结尾讲到集合相等。课本定义看起来很简单：两个集合相等，就是彼此都是对方的子集。但要形式化这句话，我们首先要理解证明助手里的等号到底是什么意思。
beats.visualNotes: Beat 1: open in the user's style. Textbook rule first, then the real question.

lean.code:
-- Textbook set equality
-- A = B when they have the same members
--
-- In Lean, this still becomes ordinary Eq:
--   A = B

hints.text: The textbook sentence becomes two proof obligations.

beats.say:
So, equal doesn't always mean been the same atomically.
1+1 = 2 is not the same atomically because they have different expressions.
But they are mathematically the same. And this is the kind of equality we want to proof.
and equality 1 = 1 is not worth proving because both side are exactly the same, and computer can just check them without knowing any math because they are the same data structure.
But this is still super useful, because it will always show up at the end of a proof for meaningful equality
On the Lean side, we can write a equals b when both sides have the same type.
And notice, we do not implement an equality typeclass first.
Because equality sign is a built-in notation for value, just like other programming languages.
But there are still two layers here.
Definitional equality means both sides reduce to the same term.
Propositional equality is an actual statement, a equals b.
When reduction is not enough, we have to provide a proof for that statement.
So think about definition versus theorem, not axiom versus theorem.
And if you have used Mathematica, this idea is familiar.
Assignment, symbolic equality, and exact sameness use different operators.
beats.sayZh: 首先，我们要把等号这个符号和“相同”这个概念分开。在 Lean 里，只要两边类型相同，就可以写 a 等于 b，而且不需要先实现相等类型类。但这里有两个层次。定义相等表示两边归约后是同一个项，所以 rfl 能完成证明。命题相等则是一条真正的陈述，也就是 a 等于 b。当归约不够时，我们必须给这条陈述提供证明。所以更准确的类比是定义与定理，不是公理与定理。如果你用过 Mathematica，这会很熟悉：赋值、符号相等和严格相同使用不同的运算符。
beats.visualNotes: Beat 2: distinguish the equals glyph, Lean's homogeneous Eq, definitional equality, and proved propositional equality. Avoid the scanner/receipt metaphor.

-- Lean's = compares terms of one type
-- no equality typeclass is required

-- definitional: both sides reduce to one term
example (n : Nat) : n + 0 = n := rfl

-- propositional: equality needs a proof
example (n : Nat) : 0 + n = n := Nat.zero_add n

hints.text: The terms do not reduce to the same syntax, so this equality needs a theorem.

beats.say:
Now the question is, when can we even write the equals sign in Lean?
Both sides must have exactly the same type.
So two as a natural number and two as an integer cannot be compared directly.
They look like the same number to us, but Lean sees two different types.
We first cast the natural number into an integer, and then equality makes sense.
Now sets A and B both have type Set alpha.
So A equals B is a valid statement, and again, no equality typeclass is needed.
But how do we prove it?
Set dot ext says, do not compare the entire set all at once.
Pick any x.
If x belongs to A exactly when x belongs to B, for every x, then the two sets are equal.
And in our textbook, this is exactly mutual subset.
beats.sayZh: 现在的问题是，什么时候我们才能在 Lean 里写等号？两边必须具有完全相同的类型。所以 Nat 里的 2 和 Int 里的 2 不能直接比较。对我们来说它们像同一个数字，但 Lean 看见的是两个类型。先把 Nat 转成 Int，等式才有意义。集合 A 和 B 都具有 Set α 类型，所以 A 等于 B 是合法陈述，而且同样不需要相等类型类。但要怎么证明？Set.ext 的意思是，不要一次比较整个集合。任选一个 x。如果对每个 x，它属于 A 当且仅当属于 B，那么两个集合相等。在我们的课本里，这正好就是互相包含。
beats.visualNotes: Beat 3: explain homogeneous equality and Set.ext from first principles. Show the cross-type counterexample, then same-members and mutual-subset equivalence.

lean.code:
-- Equality is homogeneous: both sides need one type
-- invalid: (2 : Nat) = (2 : Int)
example : ((2 : Nat) : Int) = (2 : Int) := rfl

-- Set.ext turns whole-set equality into membership
example {A B : Set α}
    (h : ∀ x, x ∈ A ↔ x ∈ B) : A = B :=
  Set.ext h

-- Same set, explained without Lean vocabulary

-- ask every possible element x:
--   x in A exactly when x in B
--
-- equivalently:
--   Subset(A, B) and Subset(B, A)

beats.say:
Now Turn-Lang makes a different choice.
We do not want to use the equals sign everywhere, and silently assume every structure has the same meaning of equality.
So look at the at-notation here.
It binds the visible A equals B to a named relation called SetEq.
That means the equals sign is only the notation.
SetEq is the actual mathematical meaning.
And when we unfold SetEq, we get exactly two goals.
A subset B.
And B subset A.
Later for functions, we can reuse the same equals sign, but bind it to FunctionEq instead.
So this is intentional overloading.
We choose the relation first, and then we choose the notation.
beats.sayZh: 现在 Turn-Lang 做了另一种选择。我们不希望到处使用等号，然后默默假设每种结构里的相等都具有同一个含义。看这里的 at-notation。它把画面上的 A 等于 B 绑定到一个叫 SetEq 的具名关系。所以等号只是记号，SetEq 才是真正的数学含义。展开 SetEq 后正好得到两个目标：A 是 B 的子集，以及 B 是 A 的子集。以后到了函数，我们可以继续使用同一个等号，但把它绑定到 FunctionEq。这是有意的重载。我们先选择关系，然后再选择记号。
beats.visualNotes: Beat 4: contrast Lean's universal homogeneous Eq with Turn's explicit notation-backed SetEq relation. Emphasize that the glyph is syntax and the named relation carries meaning.

lean.code:
-- Lean has one homogeneous Eq
-- Set extensionality supplies the bridge
--
-- A = B  ↔  A ⊆ B ∧ B ⊆ A
--
-- the theorem chooses how to prove Eq

hints.text: Here '=' is notation for the named SetEq relation, whose meaning is both subset directions.

beats.say:
Next, functions have the same kind of problem.
Two functions can be written using completely different code.
But if every input gives the same output, mathematically we want to treat them as the same function.
On the Lean side, funext turns this pointwise statement into function equality.
So for every x, prove f of x equals g of x, and then Lean gives us f equals g.
On the Turn side, we name this relation FunctionEq.
And again, the visible equals sign is attached by notation.
So the relation tells us exactly which observation must agree, the output on every input.
beats.sayZh: 接下来，函数也有同样的问题。两个函数可以用完全不同的代码写出来。但如果每个输入都得到相同输出，数学上我们希望把它们看成同一个函数。在 Lean 这边，funext 把逐点相同变成函数相等。所以对每个 x，证明 f(x) 等于 g(x)，Lean 就给出 f 等于 g。在 Turn 这边，我们把这个关系命名为 FunctionEq。同样，画面上的等号由记号绑定。这个关系明确告诉我们需要比较什么，也就是每个输入上的输出。
beats.visualNotes: Beat 5: function equality in the same spoken style.

lean.code:
-- Function equality receipt
-- funext :
--   (∀ x, f x = g x) → f = g
--
-- same output on every input

beats.say:
Finally, let's move one level higher.
In category theory, we have to be very careful not to say two objects are literally equal, when what we really mean is isomorphic.
For example, two groups can use completely different underlying elements.
So as raw data, they are not equal.
But if there is an isomorphism that preserves multiplication, identity, and inverse, then from the group theory perspective, they have the same structure.
And this connects back to everything we just did.
For sets, we compare members.
For functions, we compare outputs.
For structured objects, we compare structure-preserving maps.
And in higher category theory, even those maps can have higher comparisons.
In homotopy type theory, equality proofs behave like paths.
So the real question is not only, are these two things equal?
The real question is, at which level of mathematics should we treat them as the same?
So that is the real lesson of equality.
Next clip, we finally move to the empty set.
beats.sayZh: 最后，我们再往高一层。在范畴论里必须非常小心，不要在真正想表达同构时，说两个对象字面相等。例如两个群可以使用完全不同的底层元素。所以作为原始数据，它们并不相等。但如果存在一个保持乘法、单位元和逆元的同构，那么从群论角度看，它们具有相同结构。这和前面的内容连接起来：集合比较成员，函数比较输出，带结构的对象比较保持结构的映射。在高阶范畴论里，甚至这些映射之间还可以继续比较。在同伦类型论里，相等证明表现得像路径。所以真正的问题不只是“这两个东西相等吗”，而是“在数学的哪个层次上，我们应该把它们看作相同”。这就是相等真正的重点。下一期，我们终于进入空集。
beats.visualNotes: Beat 6: present the higher-category philosophy without naming a person. Connect members, outputs, isomorphisms, and higher equivalence; finish with two differently presented but isomorphic groups.

lean.code:
-- Choose the level of sameness
--
-- sets:      same members
-- functions: same outputs
-- groups:    structure-preserving isomorphism
-- HoTT:      equality proofs behave like paths
--
-- equivalent structure need not be identical raw data

hints.text: Two presentations can differ as data while preserving all group structure.

turn.code:
-- Ask which observations must agree
--
-- membership  -> SetEq
-- outputs     -> FunctionEq
-- structure   -> Isomorphism
-- higher maps -> higher equivalence
--
-- sameness depends on the mathematical perspective
